text:
Winnipeg scored with one second left in regulation, and that was the only way this game was going to end in their favor. Kyle Connor's wrist shot at 19:00 of the third period made it 3-2, his second goal of the night, in a game where Colorado had the better of nearly every stretch. The Avalanche carried 2.84 expected goals to Winnipeg's 2.02 and attempted 68 shots to the Jets' 50. Across a thousand replays of every shot, Colorado wins about 65 percent of them.

The gap came from the crease. Stuart Skinner faced 34 shots and stopped them at a rate better than the chances deserved, saving roughly 0.84 goals above expected, which earned him first star. Mackenzie Blackwood saw only 19 shots, but three got through against an expected 2.02, costing Colorado nearly a goal. Colorado dominated the first period, 1.03 expected goals to 0.31, and had nothing on the board for it. Jaden Schwartz finally broke through 2:51 into the second, and Connor answered 70 seconds later on a tip-in that carried just an 8 percent chance. Cole Perfetti's deflection late in the period put Winnipeg ahead.

Fedor Svechkov tied it with a tip-in at 12:35 of the third, set up by Schwartz, and the final period was dead even on chances (0.74 to 0.73). That is how a game Colorado controlled came down to one Winnipeg possession. Connor finished with four shots and 0.44 individual expected goals, scoring on 13 percent and 8 percent chances, and Mark Scheifele assisted on the winner. Neither team scored on the power play.
